title.narrative: Intergraded Child Protection and Reintegration Support for Conflict-Affected Children in Beletweyne, Hiran Region.

description.narrative: ltpgtThe escalation of military activities in Beletweyne, especially from 2022 onward, has led to substantial territorial shifts, displacement of civilian populations, and power vacuums in areas previously controlled by armed groups. While these offensives aim to dismantle extremist infrastructure, they have inadvertently increased the vulnerability of children in frontline and newly liberated areas. One of the most alarming consequences has been the surge in recruitment and use of children by armed actors both by extremist groups and occasionally by local militias mobilized to support operations. Boys, especially adolescents aged 13 to 17, are targeted for combat roles, spying, logistical support, and indoctrination. Girls are often subjected to gender-based violence and used for forced labor or marriage within armed groups. Clan militias, despite their community-based nature, have also been reported to mobilize underage boys under the guise of local defense.ltbrgtThis integrated Child Protection project targets 3,000 conflict-affected children in Beletweyne, Hiraan region, with community-based services including case management, psychosocial support (PSS), family tracing and reunification (FTR), and community-based reintegration of Children Associated with Armed Forces and Armed Groups (CAFAAG). The project prioritizes mobile delivery, use of existing community structures, and strengthened Community-Based Child Protection Mechanisms (CBCPMs) to ensure access, continuity, and safety. While the project does not provide direct GBV response services, it will integrate GBV risk mitigation, awareness, and referrals to appropriate partners. This intervention aligns with the SHF allocation strategy by delivering life-saving CP services to vulnerable children in hard-to-reach, conflict-affected areas, while ensuring convergence with ongoing SHF-funded WASH, Nutrition, Health, and Food Security activities. lt/pgtltpgtObjectives lt/pgtltpgt Provide case management to 3,000 children, including registration, care planning, and referrals. lt/pgtltpgt Reintegrate up to 900 CAFAAGs (30%) through life skills, family support, and community-based mechanisms. lt/pgtltpgt Deliver PSS to children and caregivers through group, individual, and peer sessions. lt/pgtltpgt Trace and reunify separated/unaccompanied children or place them in alternative care. lt/pgtltpgt Raise awareness on GBV risks and ensure referrals to specialized actors. lt/pgtltpgt Conduct situation monitoring through CBCPMs and mobile teams. lt/pgtltpgtTarget Beneficiaries (SADD) lt/pgtltpgt 0–4 years: 153 boys, 147 girls lt/pgtltpgt 5–9 years: 255 boys, 245 girls lt/pgtltpgt 10–14 years: 408 boys, 392 girls lt/pgtltpgt 15–17 years: 306 boys, 294 girls lt/pgtltpgt Total: 1,530 boys, 1,470 girls → 3,000 children lt/pgtltpgtActivity Breakdown by Component lt/pgtltpgt Case Management: 30% lt/pgtltpgt PSS: 15% lt/pgtltpgt FTR: 10% lt/pgtltpgt CAFAAG Reintegration: 30% lt/pgtltpgt GBV Risk Mitigation Referrals: 10% lt/pgtltpgt Situation Monitoring: 5% lt/pgtltpgtService Delivery Modalities lt/pgtltpgt Mobile CP teams for outreach and case management lt/pgtltpgt Strengthening CBCPMs and community focal points lt/pgtltpgt Use of safe spaces for group PSS (schools, health posts, halls) lt/pgtltpgt CAFAAG reintegration based on community toolkit (no centers) lt/pgtltpgt Referral pathways to GBV and health services lt/pgtltpgtConvergence with SHF-Funded Sectors lt/pgtltpgtThe project is integrated with SHF-funded Health, Nutrition, WASH, and Food Security activities in 10 mobile and outreach sites: Baacadbuke, Dabeyl, Dhaaywabar, Dharkeynta, Donsubagle, Farlibax, Nimcaan, Qooqane, Qoydo, and Shinile. This convergence: lt/pgtltpgt Enhances early identification and referral of at-risk and separated children. lt/pgtltpgt Ensures multi-Sectoral support for children lt/pgtltpgt Builds a protective environment lt/pgtltpgt Improves sustainability and efficiency by leveraging shared infrastructure and outreach mechanisms. lt/pgtltpgtSituation Monitoring Coordination lt/pgtltpgt Regular monitoring through community focal points lt/pgtltpgt Analysis of child protection risks and trends lt/pgtltpgt Participation in inter-cluster coordination forums lt/pgtltpgt Joint field visits and service mapping with other sectorslt/pgt
